reasoning: Everyday word, so ق is a glottal stop, with a long ii before it. Used of a football team or a work team.
Emphasis from the ط spreads through the word and blocks the raising of the taa marbuta, so a not e. A Turkish loan, invariable: khubz Taaza, bayDaat Taaza.
Taa marbuta after د is e. The feminine counting word and also the pronoun-like one, as in wa7de min Sa7baati.
The hamza on the alif seat is not romanized, so a3lam. Said to close a question nobody can answer.
ق is a glottal stop and both vowels are short i in the Palestinian shape. Day to day you hear 'aliil adab at least as often.
b- present, feminine you-form with the -i ending, and 7jaab starts on a cluster. The question mark is not romanized.
ذ is z in this everyday verb, so it is respelled كزب, with two short i vowels. The related noun kizbe and the adjective kazzaab show the same z.
Accurate Arabic for a bag, but a Ramallah speaker packing for a trip says shanTa, not 7a'iibe. If said at all it comes out with a glottal ق and a final e.
Country name, stressed on the first syllable with no long vowels. No article.
humme is the Palestinian they, with a doubled m and final e. The broken plural tawaa'im is bookish, though; in Ramallah you hear humme twaam or humme to'aam.
ظ is written TH. In the circumstance sense it nearly always turns up in the plural, THuruuf; the same singular also means an envelope.
One syllable with a short u, feminine sukhne. Of food, drink or water, as against shoob for hot weather.
ث is t in Palestinian, so it is respelled أكترية, with the doubled y of the -iyye ending. aghlabiyye is equally common for a majority.
Palestinian has dibbaane with د and a doubled b, not the MSA dhubaaba, so it is respelled. Collective dibbaan, one fly dibbaane.
First person b- present with ba- and a glottal ق. The second verb is bare subjunctive, with the masculine object -ak.
Dialectal relative illi and Saar for happened. bi plus the article before the moon letter alif gives bil-aakhir, with the hamza swallowed into the long aa.
ذ is d here and the first vowel drops, so it is respelled دراع with an initial cluster. In practice iid often covers the whole arm as well.

romanization: ya bakht miin baka w Di7ik
reasoning: In speech the من of this saying is miin, so it is respelled مين. Di7ik has emphatic ض and two short i vowels; ya bakht is the Palestinian lucky is.
Active participle with a long aa. Palestinian uses it where English uses a present tense: ana 3aarif I know.
Emphatic ص as S, one syllable. Shop word for a price reduction; the same form also means a deduction or an opponent.
Word-initial hamza on an alif seat is not romanized, so inta with a final a. Feminine is inti.
ع is a moon letter so the article stays il-, and the final ق is a glottal stop in ordinary speech. The country name always carries the article.

meaning_fix: granted success (of God) / brought two sides together, reconciled
reasoning: Form II with a shadda on the ف and a glottal ق. It is transitive, so the person is not the one who succeeds; allah waffa'o means God made him succeed.
Emphatic ص and a shadda doubling the ل. The ordinary verb for repairing a car, a tap or a phone.
Long uu in the first syllable, then a y glide and a. Country name, no article.
